case.summary: Customer C07297 reported an unauthorized $482.12 online purchase on November 21, 2016. Investigation revealed 4 coordinated transactions totaling $1,906.07 within 30 minutes, each deliberately priced just under $500 to evade authorization thresholds. This structuring pattern matches 5 prior closed fraud cases, and transactions originated from 2 distinct device profiles across 2 regions, indicating a compromised card. Fraud is confirmed at 0.9 probability. The card has been blocked, a case created, and the matter escalated to analyst review per Policy R9.

sar.narrative: Customer C07297, holding card C07297-K1, experienced 4 unauthorized online purchases totaling $1,906.07 on November 21, 2016, between 20:00 and 20:30. The customer reported the $482.12 transaction as unauthorized, triggering investigation. The transactions consisted of: $478.95 at 20:00 from region 264.0, $456.96 at 20:10 from region 476.0, $488.04 at 20:24 from region 476.0, and $482.12 at 20:30 from region 264.0. Each purchase was conducted online and deliberately structured to remain just below the $500 authorization threshold, indicating intentional evasion of control mechanisms. The transactions originated from 2 distinct device profiles—Windows 7 with Internet Explorer 11 and iOS with mobile Safari—suggesting the card credentials were compromised and used across multiple platforms. This pattern of multiple online purchases of amounts just under $500 within a concentrated time window matches an undocumented fraud pattern identified in 5 prior closed cases (CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907, CC-4086, CC-4124), indicating systematic fraudulent activity targeting authorization thresholds. The card has been blocked to prevent further fraud and the investigation escalated per Policy R9.
